decision.summary: A rotten-egg smell from the boiler is a possible gas leak, so this is an emergency even though the tenant said it was "not urgent", and an 82-year-old guest is staying in the flat. The tenant was told to leave, avoid switches and flames, and call 0800 111 999. JOB-101 was opened, HeatRight Ltd was asked to attend tonight, the landlord was told, and P1 escalation ESC-105 was raised for the on-call team to confirm attendance.

answers.question: 1. What severity is this and why, given the tenant says it is "not urgent"?
answers.answer: Emergency. A rotten-egg smell from a gas boiler is the standard sign of a gas leak, and the tenant's "not urgent" tone does not change that. An 82-year-old guest is also in the property.

answers.question: 2. What exactly do you tell the tenant right now, and in what order?
answers.answer: 1) Open windows and doors and leave the flat with everyone, including the guest. 2) Do not use light switches, lighters, candles or electrical appliances, and do not restart the boiler. 3) From outside, call 0800 111 999 (free, 24 hours), or 999 if unwell. 4) An engineer is being arranged and you will be messaged with details. Tell us once you are safe.

answers.question: 3. Which actions do you take tonight (job, contractor, escalation, landlord)?
answers.answer: Opened JOB-101 as an emergency gas job (A1). Messaged the tenant with safety advice (A2). Sent HeatRight Ltd an emergency call-out request (A4). Told the landlord, Ben Hartley, and explained the make-safe goes ahead without approval (A3). Escalated P1 to the on-call maintenance team (A5). Did not assign a contractor or book a visit time, because none is confirmed. Work beyond make-safe waits for landlord approval above £300 inc VAT.

actions_claimed.description: Opened emergency gas job JOB-101 for P-201 (linked to R-4801).
Sent the tenant safety advice: leave, no switches or flames, call 0800 111 999.
Told the landlord Ben Hartley about the suspected gas leak and the emergency make-safe.
Sent HeatRight Ltd an emergency gas call-out request for tonight.

conflicts: The CRM marks the tenant as not vulnerable, but the WhatsApp message says an 82-year-old is staying in the flat. I treated the occupancy as vulnerable for safety purposes and flagged it for the on-call team.
The tenant describes the issue as "not urgent", but the symptom is a gas-leak sign. Safety took priority over her description.
assumptions: A rotten-egg smell is treated as a possible gas leak until a Gas Safe engineer says otherwise.
HeatRight Ltd (C-11) is the preferred boiler contractor per the landlord's notes and is out of hours.
The emergency make-safe is allowed without landlord approval under the emergency exception in policy.

args.body:
Hi Amelia, thanks for telling us. A rotten-egg smell from the boiler can mean a gas leak, so we are treating this as an emergency, even though it is out of hours. Please do this now:
1. Open the windows and doors and leave the flat with everyone in it, including your flatmate's mum.
2. Don't use any light switches, lighters, candles or electrical appliances, and don't start the boiler again.
3. From outside, call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999 (free, 24 hours). If you can't get through or you feel unwell, call 999.
We are arranging a gas engineer to attend as soon as possible and will message you with the details. Once you are safe, please let us know you have left the property.
